audit_items.proof_trace: All price-consuming code paths go through `check_price` which asserts freshness (age ≤ price_delay_tolerance_ms) before returning a value; non-liquidation borrow-safety functions use `get_price_with_check` (EMA staleness + spot staleness + EMA/spot divergence gate), while liquidation paths intentionally use `get_price` (EMA + staleness) or `get_spot_price` (spot + staleness) so that liquidations cannot be blocked by an attacker artificially widening the EMA/spot spread. The asymmetry is a deliberate design choice, not a gap, and the property is typed as an architectural assumption confirming the Pyth oracle trust boundary.
